text: We finally get flying cars, and somehow that's fascist too. Imagine being so poisoned by the internet that you can’t enjoy anything anymore.

I remember sitting around a campfire shortly after the Ukraine war had just started with some Ukrainian friends.

They shared that after they learned that Russian forces were jamming all communications they called Elon begging for Starlink support.

Elon and the Starlink team instantly dropped everything they were working on, loaded a private jet with as many Starlink terminals as they could (terminals were in short supply at the time), and started flying the jet eastward while writing code to make terminals work over Ukraine.

There was no contract or promise of payment for doing so, and no time to solve for that.

My Ukrainian friends believed this saved the nation of Ukraine, and that without this effort Ukraine would have lost the war nearly instantly.

Ben Horowitz's message to early-stage founders on betting on yourself, the doubts that do the most damage, and why fear means you're doing it right:

"Your job is to make your bet pay off. You believed in yourself enough to do it. There are gonna be many times when you question that bet and you question that belief, but that gets you nothing."

"The doubts are gonna be there. Ignore the doubts. The worst doubts aren't the ones people put on you. It's the ones that you put on yourself. Every entrepreneur has them."

"I spent a lot of time with Mark Zuckerberg when he was 22 years old and he had a tremendous doubt about whether he was gonna make it."

$NVDA Jensen Huang on photonics: adding scale-up to optical domain, “is going to be, well, 15x” to aggregate volume.

Relating to $LITE, $COHR, and laser companies.. 

“I'm fairly certain the amount of optics that we need in the future will be several orders of magnitude” Huang added.

We’re already in a CW laser bottleneck, but given the time/rate for capacity expansion, I definitely don’t see it meeting the scale Jensen envisions…

Your leading merchant suppliers focusing new capacity toward UHP CPO lasers might also unintentionally make shortages around lower end ranges more severe…

Since even if you don’t reallocate capacity (which Coherent implied they’d do to maximize margins), the demand for lower end ranges increase too as pluggable demand grows.

Anyway, you’re gonna need a lot of lasers and given low BOM cost… this might trigger some fun game theory allocation wars + price hikes for supply

@aleabitoreddit Could you kindly elaborate on Jensen’s comment that capital is scarce in relation to impact on $SIVE. It seems they are aiming for tier 2 hyperscaler deployments and not the $LITE etc lanes. Will capital scarcity impact players like $SIVE more so then?
@aleabitoreddit Good for $AAOI too I assume?
@aleabitoreddit What about AXT?

$AAOI is the perfect example. They're expanding laser manufacturing at 350%. 

But they said they can't produce enough lasers to even meet their own pluggable transceiver demand. So they had to turn away hyperscalers for CPO lasers. 

TBH if I were AOI, I'd reallocate toward CPO lasers and then buy lasers off merchant players like $SIVE.

But I guess they want to be end-to-end vertically integrated.

$AXTI still the chokepoint of the entire optical buildout + demand for InP substrates will grow a lot. 

They have LTA supply agreements to $LITE / $COHR and probably ends up #1 vs. Sumitomo Electric.

The main thing I'm watching is if they can pull a $SNDK style price hike. So far from some channel checks: 

- Q2 2026: 50-60% increase
- Q3 2026: 10% increase
- Q4 2026: 10%+ hike

But from Coherent's SEC offering... it does look like there's a ceiling to how high % prices can go, which makes that case less likely. 

We'll see how it plays out

Few things:

- $SIVE is targeting T1 hyperscaler deployments for pluggables, CPO, NPO. Not quite sure what you mean by Tier 2. 

They have direct engagements with hyperscalers but currently are more upstream by qualifying with companies like Ayar, $JBL, $GFS, O-Net that eventually likely ends up -> $AMZN / $MSFT for example. 

On financing: 

- Colo players like $CIFR still need $1B+ of financing for their sites.
- Neoclouds like $CRWV need billions of financing to buy GPUs.

Higher rates + less support for financing makes it more challenging for these players. 

$SIVE already raised 700M SEK for their buildout and largely rely on external foundries, so they don't have financing constraints. 

There's pressure on players that need currently need financing for capex, but markets group up everyone in AI sector indiscriminately. 

The second nuance is whether or not this effects the end customers in terms of demand. 

I'd argue optical sector is insulated, even if overall AI capex from hyperscalers decreases, I see optical content still rising and aggregate demand rising. 

And this is especially the case with new incoming players going through their first qual cycles.
